newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks continue buoyant on local demand.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks continue buoyant on local demand.

text.p: Zimbabwean stocks remained buoyant on Tuesday as local institutional investors continued deserting the money market -- where interest rates have been low -- to chase higher gains in equities.
The key 57-counter industrial index leapt 104.44 points, or one percent, to close at 10,278.46.
"The market continued firm with locals the main buyers while foreigners were net sellers. We expect it to go up steadily for the rest of the week," one broker said.

Leading the day's winners, merchant bankers FMB surged 200 cents to 6,000 and blue-chip beverages and supermarkets conglomerate Delta rose 100 cents to 4,500 as did bankers Barclays to 3,600. Sugar producer Hippo and soft drinks manufacturer Schweppes gained 25 cents each to 1,525 and 335 respectively.

House appliances firm Capri at 160, tyre manufacturer Dunlop at 230 and construction group J and F at 310 all added 10 cents while horticulture company Ariston and hotel chain Zimsun traded in reasonable turnover at previous levels.

Against the trend, farm implements-maker Zimplow dropped 110 cents to 590, food company Natfoods shed 25 cents, rubber products manufacturer Acacia, engineering group Gulliver and tobacco counter TSL each lost 10 cents to 320, 230 and 790 respectively.
Minings were easier with gold producer Rio Tinto dropping 50 cents to 2,750 and nickel miner Bindura trading 15 cents down at 845.
The seven-share mining index lost 12.46 points to 1,036.10.
